title: Mandalay is quieter than Yangon
title_target: မန္တလေးက ရန်ကုန်ထက် ပိုငြိမ်တယ် — maⁿ-da.lay:-ga. yaⁿ-kohⁿ-htèk poh-ngyayⁿ-dè
goal: Comparing two things and naming the "most" — with one small marker that does the job of "than" and, as usual, stands at the back.
bekal: comparing two things with …ထက် ပို…တယ်
naming the "most" with အ…ဆုံး
saying "as … as" and "the same" with …လောက် and အတူတူ
saying what you prefer with …ပိုကြိုက်တယ်

dialogs.title: စကားပြော — Planning a weekend trip
dialogs.intro: Ko Zaw and Ani compare a few places before choosing where to go. Notice that the comparison marker ထက် stands **after** the thing being compared against, in line with the Burmese habit you already know.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ဒီအပတ်|dee-a.pak] [ဘယ်|bè] [သွား|thwa:] [ချင်|hchiⁿ] [လဲ|lè:]။ [ပုဂံ|ba.gaⁿ] [လား|la:] [မန္တလေး|maⁿ-da.lay:] [လား|la:]။
lines.id: Where do you want to go this week? Bagan or Mandalay?
lines.literal: week-this — where — go — want — Q? bagan — or — mandalay — or?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [နှစ်ခု|hna.hkoo.] [လုံး|lohⁿ:] [မ|ma.] [ရောက်|yowk] [ဖူး|hpoo:] [ဘူး|boo:]။ [ဘယ်ဟာ|bè-ha] [က|ga.] [ပို|poh] [ကောင်း|kowⁿ:] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: I've never been to either. Which one is better?
lines.literal: two-things — all — not — arrive — ever — not. which-thing — the — more — be-good — Q?

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ပုဂံ|ba.gaⁿ] [က|ga.] [မန္တလေး|maⁿ-da.lay:] [ထက်|htèk] [ပို|poh] [လှ|hla.] [တယ်|dè]။ [ဘုရား|hpa.ya:] [နှစ်ထောင်|hna.htowⁿ] [လောက်|lowk] [ရှိ|shee.] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: Bagan is more beautiful than Mandalay. There are about two thousand pagodas.
lines.literal: bagan — the — mandalay — than — more — be-beautiful — statement. pagoda — two-thousand — about — be — statement.

lines.text: [နှစ်ထောင်|hna.htowⁿ]! [ဝေး|way:] [လား|la:]။

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [မန္တလေး|maⁿ-da.lay:] [ထက်|htèk] [ပို|poh] [ဝေး|way:] [တယ်|dè]။ [ကားနဲ့|ka:-nè.] [ဆယ်|hsay] [နာရီ|na-yee] [လောက်|lowk] [ကြာ|cha] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: Farther than Mandalay. About ten hours by car.

lines.text: [တစ်နာရီခွဲ|ta.na-yee-hkwè:] [ပဲ|bè:]။ [ဒါပေမဲ့|da-bay-mè.] [ကား|ka:] [ထက်|htèk] [အများကြီး|a.mya:-chee:] [ပို|poh] [ဈေးကြီး|zay:-chee:] [တယ်|dè]။

grammars.title: …ထက် ပို…တယ် — more … than
body: A comparison is built from two parts: **ထက်** (*htèk*) attaches to the thing you compare against, and **ပို** (*poh*) stands in front of the quality. The order: A — B ထက် — ပို — quality — တယ်.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: ပုဂံက မန္တလေးထက် ပိုလှတယ်
Bagan is more beautiful than Mandalay
ဒါက ဟိုဟာထက် ပိုကောင်းတယ်
ကားထက် ပိုဈေးကြီးတယ်
ဘယ်ဟာက ပိုကောင်းလဲ

after: ⚠️ The thing compared against can be **dropped** when it's clear from context: ပိုကောင်းတယ် on its own already means "it's better". This is used all the time and makes your sentences much shorter.
To stress the difference, slot အများကြီး (*a.mya:-chee:*, "much") in before ပို: အများကြီး ပိုဈေးကြီးတယ် — "much more expensive".

grammars.title: အ…ဆုံး — most
body: The "most" form wraps around the adjective: the prefix **အ** in front and **ဆုံး** (*hsohⁿ:*) behind. The result works both as a noun and as a description.
after: To say what something is the most among, use the marker **ထဲမှာ** ("in, among"): မြန်မာပြည်ထဲမှာ အကြီးဆုံး မြို့ (the biggest city in Myanmar). Once again, the description stands in front of the noun.

grammars.title: …လောက် — as … as
body: To say two things are equal, use လောက် (*lowk*) — the same word that means "about" in unit 5. In everyday use it almost always comes with a negative.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: ရန်ကုန်လောက် မစည်ဘူး
ဒါလောက် မကောင်းဘူး

after: ⚠️ Notice that "not as lively as Yangon" uses လောက် **without** ပို. Adding ပို to a negative sentence like this sounds odd — ပို is only used when something really is "more".

grammars.title: …လည်း…တယ် — both … and …
body: This repetition pattern says that two qualities apply at once, and it has a very Burmese conversational ring. The adjective is said twice, with လည်း in between.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
rows: ငြိမ်လည်း ငြိမ်တယ်
လှလည်း လှတယ်
ကောင်းလည်း ကောင်းတယ်

after: English has a faint echo of this in "it's cheap, I'll give it that" or "quiet? quiet all right". Use it just once in a conversation and the other person will stop and ask how long you've been learning.

blocks.text: The twenty adjectives below cover most everyday conversation. Remember, they're all verbs — so they all take the ending တယ်, are negated with မ … ဘူး, and are compared with ပို.

blocks.title: ပုဂံ — two thousand pagodas on one plain
items: **ပုဂံ** (*ba.gaⁿ*, Bagan) was the capital of the first Burmese kingdom, and on a plain of forty square kilometers stand more than two thousand temples and stupas built between the 11th and 13th centuries — around the same era as Angkor in Cambodia.
Its kings built for a reason shared across Buddhist Southeast Asia: raising sacred buildings to gather **ကုသိုလ်** (*koo.thoh*, merit) — from the Pali word *kusala*, "wholesome".

⚠️ Since 2016, climbing the temples in Bagan has been **banned** after an earthquake damaged many of them. To watch the sunrise, go up the viewing mounds set aside for it; climbing a temple can mean a fine and, more importantly, is seen as deeply disrespectful.
